sections.title: Detailed Brief Overview
rows: **Revolutionary Movements & Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose** - Militant nationalism, secret societies, and the armed struggle for India's complete independence.
**1897 to 1945** - Phase 1 (Early Revolutionary Societies: 1897-1915), Phase 2 (Socialist-leaning Revolutionaries: 1924-1935), and Netaji's Phase (1938-1945).
**Key Figures:** Vasudev Balwant Phadke, Khudiram Bose, Prafulla Chaki, Bhagat Singh, Chandrashekhar Azad, Rash Behari Bose, and **Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose**.
Challenged British colonial rule directly through armed force, awakening national consciousness and accelerating the transfer of power.
Secret societies, bomb-making, political dacoities to fund arms, individual heroism, mass mobilization via the Indian National Army (INA).
**Phase I (Maharashtra & Bengal terrorism)**, **Phase II (HRA/HSRA socialist revolutionaries)**, and **INA/Azad Hind Government**.
High-scoring static GK area in UP Assistant Teacher exam covering specific dates, founding members of secret societies, journals, and INA campaigns.
Concentrated primarily in **Bengal, Maharashtra, Punjab, Uttar Pradesh (UP)**, and later South-East Asia (Singapore, Japan).

items.title: Phase I: Early Revolutionary Movements (1897-1915)
items.content:
• **Ramosi Peasant Force (1879):** Founded by **Vasudev Balwant Phadke** in Maharashtra, considered the pioneer of armed resistance.
• **Anushilan Samiti (1902):** Founded in Calcutta by **Promotha Mitra**, with prominent leaders like **Barindra Kumar Ghosh** and **Jatindranath Banerjee**.
• **Abhinav Bharat (1904):** Reorganized by **Vinayak Damodar Savarkar (VD Savarkar)** from Mitra Mela in Nashik.
• **Alipore Conspiracy Case (1908):** Attempted assassination of Judge Kingsford by **Khudiram Bose** and **Prafulla Chaki**.
• **Mnemonic for Founders:** **V**asudev (**R**amosi), **V**D Savarkar (**A**bhinav Bharat) -> **'Very Valuable Animals'**.

items.title: Phase II: Socialist-leaning Revolutionaries (1924-1935)
items.content:
• **Hindustan Republican Association (HRA) - 1924:** Founded in Kanpur by **Sachindra Nath Sanyal**, **Ram Prasad Bismil**, and **Jogesh Chandra Chatterjee**.
• **Kakori Conspiracy Train Robbery (August 9, 1925):** HRA members looted official train cash near Lucknow; **Ram Prasad Bismil, Ashfaqulla Khan, Roshan Singh, and Rajendra Lahiri** were hanged.
• **Hindustan Socialist Republican Association (HSRA) - 1928:** Re-established at Feroz Shah Kotla, Delhi, under the leadership of **Chandrashekhar Azad** and **Bhagat Singh**.
• **Saunders' Assassination (1928):** Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev, and Rajguru killed British police officer John Saunders to avenge **Lala Lajpat Rai's death**.
• **Central Assembly Bomb Case (1929):** Bhagat Singh and Batukeshwar Dutt threw low-intensity bombs in the Central Assembly to 'make the deaf hear'.

items.title: Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose and Early Political Career
items.content:
• **Birth & Education:** Born on **January 23, 1897**, in Cuttack, Odisha; cleared the **ICS examination** in England in 1920 but resigned to join the national movement.
• **Political Mentor:** Guided by **Deshbandhu Chittaranjan Das (CR Das)**.
• **Municipal Leadership:** Elected Mayor of Calcutta in **1930**.
• **Congress Presidency:** Elected President at **Haripura Session (1938)** and re-elected at **Tripuri Session (1939)** defeating **Gandhian candidate Pattabhi Sitaramayya**.
• **Resignation & Forward Bloc:** Resigned from Congress due to ideological differences with Mahatma Gandhi and founded the **Forward Bloc** in **1939**.

items.title: The Azad Hind Fauj (Indian National Army - INA) and Azad Hind Government
items.content:
• **Concept Origin:** Originally conceived by **Captain Mohan Singh** in Malaya in 1942 using Indian Prisoners of War (POWs).
• **Revival by Netaji:** Netaji escaped house arrest in Calcutta in 1941 (**Mahabhiniskraman**), reached Germany, and later traveled by submarine to Southeast Asia in **1943** to take command from **Rash Behari Bose**.
• **Provisional Government of Free India:** Established in Singapore on **October 21, 1943**; recognized by Axis powers.
• **Famous Slogans:** **'Dilli Chalo'** and **'Give me blood, and I shall give you freedom!'**.
• **Military Wings:** Formed regiments named after national heroes - **Gandhi Regiment, Nehru Regiment, Subhas Regiment**, and the all-women **Jhansi Regiment** led by **Captain Lakshmi Swaminathan**.

items.title: Mnemonic Masterclass for Revolutionary Trials and Dates
items.content:
• **Mnemonic for Major Conspiracy Cases (Chronological Order):** **A**lipore (1908), **H**owrah (1910), **D**elhi-Lahore (1912), **K**akori (1925), **M**eerut (1929) -> **'All Hungry Dogs Kick Meat'**.
• **Mnemonic for INA Trials Location:** All high-profile trials took place at **Red Fort, Delhi** (**1945-46**), defended by legal giants like **Bhulabhai Desai, Tej Bahadur Sapru, and Jawaharlal Nehru**.
• **Mnemonic for Netaji's Key Years:** **1938** (Haripura), **1939** (Tripuri/Forward Bloc), **1941** (Great Escape), **1943** (Singapore INA takeover) -> **'38, 39, 41, 43 — Netaji Takes Command'**.

sections.title: Important Facts and Data
rows: Founded in 1899 at Nashik; precursor to Abhinav Bharat.
Eastern Bengal revolutionary hub formed in 1906.
Founded in 1913 at San Francisco, USA; published 'Ghadar' paper.
Japanese ship carrying Indian passengers turned back from Canada in 1914.
Sachindra Nath Sanyal, Ram Prasad Bismil
Founded in 1924 at Kanpur; Marxist-socialist leaning.
Established in 1928 at Feroz Shah Kotla with socialist objectives.
April 18, 1930; led Indian Republican Army to raid British arsenal.
Founded in May 1939 as a left-wing faction within Congress.
Broadcast nationalist news to counter British propaganda.
Bhulabhai Desai, Tej Bahadur Sapru, Kailash Nath Katju
Defended INA accused (P.K. Sehgal, Shah Nawaz Khan, G.S. Dhillon) at Red Fort.

items.definition: Remember **B.A.R.R.** for the 4 martyrs hanged in Kakori: **B**ismil (Ram Prasad), **A**shfaqulla Khan, **R**oshan Singh, and **R**ajendra Lahiri.
Netaji edited and founded **'Forward'** newspaper (started by CR Das) and later **'Swaraj'**. Remember: **'Netaji moved Forward toward Swaraj'**.

Key women in Bengal revolutionaries: **Pritilata Waddedar** (Chittagong raid), **Kalpana Datta**, and **Bina Das** (shot Governor Stanley Jackson at Calcutta University convocation in 1932). Remember: **'PBC - Pritilata, Bina, Kalpana'**.

items.term: Trick 4: Bhagat Singh's Pseudonyms & Jail Fast
items.definition: Bhagat Singh wrote under the pen name **'Balwant'** and went on a **116-day hunger strike** in jail demanding equal rights for Indian prisoners compared to European inmates.

items.term: Trick 5: INA Regiments Named After Leaders
items.definition: The four main INA brigades were **Gandhi, Nehru, Azad, and Subhas**. Remember: **'GNAS'** (Gandhi-Nehru-Azad-Subhas).
Key figures: **Lala Hardayal** (Secretary/Brain), **Sohan Singh Bhakna** (President). Remember: **'Hardayal is Hard at Work, Bhakna is the Boss'**.
**HRA** was founded in **1924** in Kanpur by Sachindra Sanyal and Ram Prasad Bismil. **HSRA** was founded in **1928** in Delhi with 'Socialist' added by Bhagat Singh and Chandrashekhar Azad.
Students often think Netaji founded the INA from scratch. **Captain Mohan Singh** originally founded the INA in 1942; Netaji took over its leadership in **1943**.
Netaji won the 1939 Tripuri presidential election against **Pattabhi Sitaramayya** (backed by Gandhi), NOT Jawaharlal Nehru or Vallabhbhai Patel.
Chittagong Armoury Raid (1930) was led by **Surya Sen (Masterda)**, NOT Subhas Chandra Bose or Bhagat Singh.
**Aurobindo Ghosh** was arrested in the Alipore Bomb Case (1908) but was defended brilliantly by **Chittaranjan Das** and acquitted due to lack of evidence.
The Provisional Government of Free India headquarters was located in **Singapore and Rangoon (Myanmar)**, NOT in Tokyo, Japan.
Triggered by the **1905 Partition of Bengal**, giving birth to swadeshi, boycott, and secret revolutionary societies in Bengal and Maharashtra.
Premier secret societies of Bengal that published **'Jugantar'** weekly advocating armed revolution against British officials.
HRA operation to loot government treasury money; led to capital punishment for four major revolutionary stalwarts.
Shifted from mere terrorism to socialist revolution under Bhagat Singh, incorporating Marxist principles and mass peasant-worker awakening.
Combined radical nationalism with social democracy and economic planning; firmly believed India needed complete Purna Swaraj immediately.
Marked ideological parting of ways between Gandhi's pacifist approach and Bose's militant demand for immediate ultimatum to the British.
Netaji escaped house arrest disguised as a Pathan named **'Mohammed Ziauddin'**, traveling via Peshawar and Kabul to Germany.
Netaji founded the **Free India Center** in Berlin and started Azad Hind Radio broadcasts in German, English, and Indian languages.
Arrived in Singapore via German and Japanese submarines; assumed supreme command of INA and Azad Hind Government.
INA marched toward India, crossed the border, and hoisted the Tricolour at **Moirang (Manipur)** with the cry **'Jai Hind'**.
Public trials at Red Fort created massive pan-Indian sympathy and sparked naval/military mutinies (Royal Indian Navy Mutiny, 1946), hastening British exit.

upscNotes.content: For the UP Assistant Teacher exam, focus heavily on match-the-following questions linking secret societies (Anushilan Samiti, Abhinav Bharat, Ghadar Party) with their founders and exact years.

Examiners often trap students by asking who founded the INA. The correct answer for founder is Captain Mohan Singh, whereas Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose is the supreme commander who revitalized and expanded it.
Remember the exact dates of the Kakori Conspiracy (August 9, 1925) and Chittagong Armoury Raid (April 18, 1930) as direct chronological questions frequently appear.
Do not confuse Netaji's Forward Bloc (1939) with the Swaraj Party (1923). Forward Bloc was a leftist faction within the INC founded after resigning from Congress presidency.
Note down the names of defense lawyers for the Red Fort INA trials: Bhulabhai Desai, Tej Bahadur Sapru, and Jawaharlal Nehru. This is a favorite factual question in UP teaching exams.

keyTakeaways: Revolutionary movements transitioned from individual terrorism and assassinations (Phase I) to socialist-oriented mass revolutionary action (Phase II under HSRA).
Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose was twice elected Congress President (Haripura 1938, Tripuri 1939) before resigning to form the Forward Bloc.
The Azad Hind Fauj (INA) established a Provisional Government of Free India in Singapore on October 21, 1943.
The Rani of Jhansi Regiment was the all-women combat regiment of the INA, led by Captain Lakshmi Swaminathan.
Netaji coined iconic slogans like 'Dilli Chalo', 'Jai Hind', and 'Give me blood, and I shall give you freedom!'.
The Red Fort trials of INA prisoners in 1945-46 ignited unprecedented nationalist fury across India, uniting Hindus, Muslims, and Sikhs against British rule.
Masterda Surya Sen led the daring Chittagong Armoury Raid of 1930, utilizing the Indian Republican Army banner.
